questions.q: What was the real name of Hashim, the Prophet's ancestor?
questions.explain: Hashim was the Prophet's ancestor, and his real name was Amr.

options: Because he crumbled bread into soup for the pilgrims
Because he was born in Yathrib
questions.explain: Hashama means to crumble bread into soup. That is how Amr came to be called Hashim.

questions.q: Who brought Shaybah from Yathrib to Makkah?
questions.explain: Al-Muttalib brought Shaybah to Makkah, and people called him Abdul Muttalib.

questions.q: What was the old name of Madinah?
questions.explain: Yathrib is the old name of Madinah.

questions.q: How did Abdul Muttalib find the well of Zamzam again?
options: Through a dream over four nights
questions.explain: After a dream over four nights, Abdul Muttalib dug where he was shown and found Zamzam.

questions.q: How many camels were given to ransom Abdullah?
questions.explain: The azlam arrow landed on the camels once a hundred had been set down, so Abdullah was saved.

questions.q: Abdul Muttalib vowed to sacrifice one son if he was given ten sons.
questions.explain: True. After the dispute over Zamzam, he vowed to sacrifice one son if he was given ten sons.
False. It was Hashim who died in Gaza. Abdullah died in Yathrib on his way back from Sham.

questions.q: Put these events in the right order.

items.text: Abdullah is ransomed with a hundred camels
Abdul Muttalib makes his vow about ten sons

questions.explain: Shaybah was brought to Makkah, Zamzam was found, the vow was made, Abdullah was ransomed, and then he married Aminah.

questions.q: Match each term with its meaning.

right.text: Arrows cast to make a decision
A promise to Allah to do something

questions.explain: Hashama is crumbling bread into soup, Yathrib is the old name of Madinah, a nazar is a promise to Allah, and azlam are arrows used to decide.

questions.q: The water ran out in the desert, but Abdul Muttalib refused to give up. What attitude can we take from this?
options: Keep trying and never give up
questions.explain: Abdul Muttalib did not give up, and Allah inspired him with the place of water.
